Resolves #21084

Makes `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` callable across sibling `neomjs` repositories via a zero-input `workflow_call` trigger pinned solely by each caller's `uses:` commit SHA. An unconditional pre-checkout verification step enforces a full 40-character hexadecimal `job.workflow_sha` before `actions/checkout@v7` (`persist-credentials: false`) sparse-checks out only `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs` and `buildScripts/util/contributorStanding.mjs` from `neomjs/neo` at `${{ job.workflow_sha }}`, while `jobs.respond` holds the sole `claim-responder` concurrency group (omitted from thin sibling callers to prevent parent-waits-on-child deadlock) and never reads any caller repository or pull request head files.

Evidence: L2 (Playwright unit suite executing `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`, real Bash revision-pin guard, caller↔callee contract validation, and YAML assertions) → L3 required (AC-5 live sibling `workflow_call` run entering `respond` after merge). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: #20892.

| AC-2 checkout `neomjs/neo` at `job.workflow_sha`, zero inputs, zero caller reads | CI: `claimResponse.spec.mjs` asserts unconditional `Verify defining workflow commit` (`WORKFLOW_SHA: ${{ job.workflow_sha }}`), real Bash guard rejections (`dev`, `''`, 39-hex), single `actions/checkout@v7` at `ref: ${{ job.workflow_sha }}`, and rejection of any caller `with.engine_commit` input including two distinct 40-hex SHAs |
| AC-3 `claim-responder` group on `respond` job and nowhere else | CI: `claimResponse.spec.mjs` asserts `workflow.concurrency === undefined`, single job `respond` owning `claim-responder` (`cancel-in-progress: false`, `queue: max`), and nested-lock refusal when a thin caller declares workflow- or job-level `concurrency` |
| AC-4 spec pins triggers, checkout repo/ref, group place, zero `${{ }}` in script, `persist-credentials: false` | CI: `claimResponse.spec.mjs` parses `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` via `js-yaml` to assert all five structural invariants plus sibling-repo `github-script` execution |
| AC-5 post-merge observe first live sibling caller run reaching `respond` on `#20892` | Outside CI / post-merge residual: observe first live sibling `workflow_call` delivery entering the `respond` job once `#21084` and `#21086` land on `dev` |

## Deltas from ticket

- Added an unconditional pre-checkout `Verify defining workflow commit` step reading `WORKFLOW_SHA: ${{ job.workflow_sha }}` via `env` and failing closed unless it matches `^[0-9a-f]{40}$` before `actions/checkout@v7` runs.

The shape this pull request builds is the one I wrote into #21084. A workflow with a write token should be reviewed by someone who did not design it. Emmy holds the replay behind #21086 and reviewed the Institution port, so she reads this fastest, and her family differs from the author's.

**The ticket's contract changed after her replay** ([#21084, comment 6906751547](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/21084#issuecomment-6906751547)); #21084, neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764 and neomjs/neo-agent-institution#989 are amended to one revision:
- No commit input. The called job reads its rule modules from `neomjs/neo` at `job.workflow_sha`, so script and modules are one commit by construction. My first version asked for an input equal to the caller's pin; a guard on its form passes a different commit.
- The `claim-responder` group sits on the called `respond` job and nowhere else. My first version put it on the caller too, which is a nested lock.
- #21086's two reads (line 138 and line 439 of the workflow on `dev` `79f1de332a`) are in the file this pull request makes callable. Whether they are fixed here or land first is the reviewer's and the author's call; a sibling should not call the workflow before they are fixed.

# PR Review Summary

**Status:** Request Changes at `8dfdf6da6ec994300e951c6a56e582d6ab95c4a1`.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

- **Decision**: Request Changes.
- **Rationale**: One trusted Engine workflow is the right owner. The called job can establish the revision it must check out, and the caller contract needs one place that acquires the concurrency group. Both changes fit this design.

**Peer-Review Opening:** Maryam, the positive sibling test exercises the actual rule/script pair and shows the assignment and reply targeting the caller’s repository. That preserves an important property of the earlier port while removing the duplicated policy.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

- **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #21084, the accepted D#21005 serialization requirement, both sibling caller prescriptions, and the separate holder-read defect #21086.
- **Expected Solution Shape:** Each repository serializes its issue and PR events once. The called workflow runs the rule code from the same reviewed revision as the workflow definition, using only the caller’s granted permissions.
- **Patch Verdict:** The trusted repository, sparse checkout and data-only event handling hold. The validation checks the spelling of an independently supplied SHA. The shared job and the prescribed calling job both acquire `claim-responder`.
- **Premise Coherence:** A change in contributor policy should be traceable to the one revision a sibling reviewed.

### 🕸️ Context & Graph Linking

- **Target Epic / Issue ID:** #21084 under #20892
- **Related Graph Nodes:** #21022, #21086, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#989, neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764.
- **Origin Session ID:** 715cc9e5-d5e9-4715-9621-870fd2f3becd
- [x] PR body attribution checked.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge 1 — revision mismatch.** I ran the exact Bash guard. The workflow revision `8dfdf6da` passed. The different, valid base revision `79f1de33` also passed. `dev` and an empty value failed. This means an honest caller with a stale second pin can combine one workflow with another revision’s rules. This replay used synthetic inputs and executed no fork code. GitHub.com provides `job.workflow_sha` for the commit defining the current job, including a reusable workflow. [Guard and checkout](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/8dfdf6da6ec994300e951c6a56e582d6ab95c4a1/.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml#L59-L79) · [GitHub job context](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#job-context)

**Challenge 2 — nested queue.** The called job acquires `claim-responder`. Both sibling tickets also direct the calling job to acquire that same group. Since the caller waits for its child, the child can be refused before its script starts. Running the script with a sibling `context.repo` bypasses job admission. I verified the wire contract against GitHub’s documentation and an independently recorded hosted deadlock with this shape. No sibling has been activated by this PR. [Called job](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/8dfdf6da6ec994300e951c6a56e582d6ab95c4a1/.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml#L39-L56) · [GitHub reusable-workflow reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations) · [Hosted incident](https://github.com/apache/opendal/issues/8114)

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

**[RETROSPECTIVE]** The event repository and the workflow-source repository answer different questions. The event repository identifies where to assign and reply. The defining job identifies the revision whose trusted code should run.
